title: Position: LLMs Can Be Good Tutors in English Education
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
extended_summary:
This position paper argues that large language models (LLMs) can function as effective tutors in English education and should be understood not merely as generic text generators, but as tools that can support pedagogy in more structured ways. The paper addresses a broad question: how LLMs can be integrated into English teaching and learning while respecting educational principles, learner needs, and classroom realities.

The authors organize their argument around three roles for LLMs. First, LLMs can serve as data enhancers by creating educational materials, reformulating existing texts, simulating students, and annotating learning data. Second, they can act as task predictors for discriminative, generative, and mixed educational tasks such as automated assessment, knowledge tracing, grammatical error correction, feedback generation, and Socratic dialogue. Third, they can operate as agents that support tutoring through knowledge integration, pedagogical alignment, planning, memory, and tool use.

The paper situates these ideas in English education contexts spanning listening, speaking, reading, and writing, with examples such as comprehension questions, pronunciation feedback, text simplification, and individualized writing support. It concludes that LLMs hold substantial promise for personalized, scalable, and inclusive English instruction, but only if they are paired with guardrails, human oversight, and stronger pedagogical alignment. The paper also emphasizes key risks, including hallucinations, bias, privacy concerns, misalignment with expert teaching practices, and the danger of overreliance on automated systems.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed position paper rather than an empirical evaluation, so it does not present a testable study design, comparison, or causal evidence. It argues for potential roles and discusses challenges, but provides no direct outcome data for K-12 learners.
impact_tier_rationale: No measured learning or implementation impact is reported, so there is no evidentiary basis for estimating effect size or practical impact. The paper is conceptual and forward-looking rather than outcome-reporting.

interventions.use_case: Position paper on using LLM tutors in English education, including conversational agents for real-time practice, scaffolding, feedback, and personalized instruction; explicitly references Khanmigo as an example of GPT-4-based educational helper.
LLM-mediated grading and formative feedback for essays, short answers, spoken language, grammatical error correction, and error analysis.
LLM-assisted English writing support such as grammar/syntax/style feedback, revision suggestions, text simplification/paraphrasing, and EFL writing education.
LLM-empowered tutoring systems that model learner history, support adaptive instruction, and deliver personalized tutoring interactions in English education.
